blockers.evidence: Official subprocess-local eagerly imports node-pty and its Windows inspector module imports koffi. The frozen Koffi 3.1.6 is post-statx-fix and has Android/Termux source-build evidence, but official support still excludes Android. node-pty v1.2.0-beta.15 has no Android support declaration; the Community NDK path must prove the unmodified package can build/load.

Official attachment-local depends on sharp. The frozen runtime lock already records sharp@0.35.4 plus exact @img/sharp-wasm32@0.35.4 and @emnapi/runtime@1.11.3; sharp's loader has a generic WASM fallback after platform-native resolution. Remaining gaps are optional-byte materialization and a real Android carrier image smoke.

Official sandbox-local PLATFORM_CHAINS defines linux, darwin, and win32 only; an unlisted platform fails closed when confinement is requested. The package also imports Landlock and Windows ACL backends.
blockers.nextProbe: Provide an Android-safe runner through the official sandbox seam or wait for upstream Android support; then test under the APK app UID.

blockers.evidence: Official DSH tool-fs-search imports @vscode/ripgrep. Wrapper 1.18.0 resolves @vscode/ripgrep-${process.platform}-${arch}, so Android requires an unpublished @vscode/ripgrep-android-* package. The official sidecar path only activates for pkg single-file runtimes.
blockers.nextProbe: Wait for an upstream Android package or an explicit official rg-path seam; any Community adapter must preserve the pinned ripgrep 15.0.0 + Microsoft v15.0.1 patch provenance and undergo separate architecture review.

conclusion: Node 22 is necessary but insufficient. The published top-level @deepseek-ai/dsh package eagerly carries the native closure, so profile-only row disabling cannot make the current official CLI package Android-safe.
